title: Gravity above the surface
target: Use distance from a planet’s center to compare fields at altitude.
criteria: Use r=R+h rather than altitude alone.
Compare fields with the inverse-square relation.
Explain why orbit is not a zero-gravity region.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A planet has radius R. A probe is at altitude 3R. What is center distance?
cpa.guide: Center distance is radius plus altitude: R + 3R = 4R.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Why is altitude alone unsuitable as r in GM/r² at the planet’s surface?
options: Altitude is zero there, but center separation is the planet’s nonzero radius.
r always means the probe’s radius.
The planet’s mass becomes zero at its surface.
cpa.guide: The inverse-square formula uses separation from the source center.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Surface field is 20 N/kg. What is field at center distance 2R in the spherical model?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A probe moves from center distance 2R to 4R. How does local g change?
options: It becomes one-quarter of its value at 2R.
cpa.guide: The relevant ratio is 4R/(2R) = 2, then inverse square.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Why can an astronaut appear weightless in orbit despite substantial gravity?
options: Gravity is exactly zero in every orbit.
The astronaut and spacecraft fall together.
cpa.guide: Shared free fall removes the usual support force sensation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: An orbiting station is only a small fraction of a planetary radius above the surface. Which claim is most plausible?
options: Gravity must be negligible solely because the station is in space.
Field strength must exceed the surface value.
Gravity remains substantial; apparent weightlessness is caused by free fall.
cpa.guide: The center-distance change is modest, so inverse-square gravity remains significant.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
